subject: Trading
title: John Templeton: The Global Pioneer
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on John Templeton: The Global Pioneer.

hook.text: In 1939, John Templeton bought $100 of every stock under a dollar on the New York Stock Exchange. He made a fortune.

buildup.text: Templeton was among the first to invest globally, buying Japanese stocks in the 1960s when no one else would.

discovery.text: His philosophy: buy at the point of 'maximum pessimism'—when fear is highest and prices are lowest.

twist.text: He moved to the Bahamas to gain distance from Wall Street's groupthink—literally separating himself from the crowd.

climax.text: Templeton proved that geographic diversification and contrarian courage could produce extraordinary long-term returns.

punchline.text: He bought when others couldn't bear to look.

quiz.question: What was Templeton's strategy for buying stocks?
options: Buy at the point of maximum pessimism when fear is highest
